article_content: The UN Security Council held a discussion on Monday on the topic of combating sexual violence in conflict zones. Two senior UN officials stated that effective measures must be taken to prevent sexual violence and abuse in conflict zones. Rajia Sultana, a lawyer for the Rohingya, said that the UN Security Council has failed to prevent the Rohingya crisis. She called on the 15 member states of the Security Council to bring the issue of sexual violence and abuse against the Rohingya to the International Criminal Court. UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Muhammad said that sexual violence and abuse have been used as a first step in military campaigns and persecution in various places, including Myanmar. UN Special Representative Pramila Patten said that the information on paper and the actual situation are not the same, and that no effective action has been taken to prevent violence against women.
